articles.title: Hong Kong Launches Its First Five-Year Plan: What It Means for You
articles.summary: Hong Kong has released its very first five-year development plan alongside the 2026 Policy Address. The plan focuses on growing the Northern Metropolis — a large area near the border with mainland China — into a major hub for education, jobs, and housing. The government also announced new support for families with babies and fresh measures to boost employment. Chief Executive Lee Ka-chiu said there are 22 key targets in the plan, five of which are binding, meaning officials must be held responsible if those goals are not met. This is a big step for Hong Kong as it tries to plan its future more carefully.

lv1: What is the name of the big development area mentioned in Hong Kong's new five-year plan? (香港新五年規劃中提到的大型發展區叫什麼名字？)
How many key targets are listed in Hong Kong's five-year plan? (香港五年規劃列出了多少個主要指標？)
lv2: Why do you think it is important for the government to have binding targets that officials can be held responsible for? (你認為政府設立具約束力的指標、讓官員承擔責任，為什麼重要？)
How might developing the Northern Metropolis help ordinary people living in Hong Kong? (發展北部都會區可以怎樣幫助香港普通市民？)
lv3: Do you think a five-year plan is the best way to manage a city's future? What are the advantages and disadvantages compared to shorter or longer planning periods? (你認為五年規劃是管理城市未來的最佳方式嗎？與較短或較長的規劃期相比，有何優缺點？)

The plan includes targets for housing and employment. Who should decide what the most important goals for a city are — the government, the citizens, or both? Explain your view. (規劃包括房屋和就業目標。誰應該決定城市最重要的目標——政府、市民還是兩者？請說明你的看法。)

articles.title: American Residents Push Back Against Giant AI Data Centres in Their Neighbourhoods
articles.summary: People living near planned artificial intelligence data centres across the United States are speaking out against the massive buildings being built close to their homes. Residents worry about noise, enormous electricity usage, and the effect on local water supplies, as these facilities need huge amounts of power and cooling water to run AI systems. Meanwhile, former US President Donald Trump has suggested that opposition to the centres is being encouraged by China, a claim that local community groups strongly deny. The debate raises important questions about who benefits from new technology and who ends up paying the price in their daily lives.

lv1: What kind of buildings are local residents in the US complaining about? (美國居民在抱怨哪種建築物？)
What are two things that AI data centres need a lot of to operate? (人工智能數據中心需要大量哪兩種資源才能運作？)
lv2: Why might local communities be unhappy about having a large data centre built near their homes, even if it brings new technology benefits? (即使大型數據中心帶來新科技好處，為什麼附近社區居民可能仍然不滿意？)
Why is it important to think about who benefits and who is harmed when new technology is introduced into a neighbourhood? (在社區引入新科技時，為什麼要考慮誰受益、誰受害是重要的？)
lv3: Should communities have the right to block technology infrastructure projects in their area, even if those projects could benefit the wider country? Discuss both sides. (社區是否應有權阻止在其地區建設科技基礎設施項目，即使該項目可能惠及更廣泛的國家？請討論雙方觀點。)

When a government or powerful figure blames a foreign country for domestic protests, how should citizens evaluate whether that claim is true? What skills do you need? (當政府或有權勢的人將國內抗議歸咎於外國時，市民應如何判斷這種說法是否屬實？你需要哪些技能？)

articles.title: 施政報告擬立法規管「深偽」罪案　李家超：保護市民免受虛假影像傷害
articles.summary: 香港行政長官李家超在2026年施政報告中表示，政府正研究以立法方式打擊「深偽技術」（Deepfake）罪案。深偽技術是指利用人工智能製造虛假影片或圖像，令人誤以為真實。李家超指出，他本人亦曾多次被不法分子用深偽技術偽造形象，強調保護市民不受虛假內容傷害是政府的重要責任。此次立法建議是香港應對人工智能帶來的新挑戰的重要一步。

lv1: 「深偽技術」是用什麼方法製造假影片的？
李家超在哪份政府文件中提出研究立法規管深偽罪案？
lv2: 為什麼深偽技術對普通市民構成威脅？請舉出一個實際例子加以說明。
政府為何認為需要以立法方式來處理深偽問題，而不是靠市民自行分辨真假？
lv3: 立法規管深偽技術有助保護市民，但同時可能限制創作自由和言論自由。你認為應如何在兩者之間取得平衡？
隨著人工智能技術日趨普及，社會上「真實」與「虛假」的界線愈來愈模糊。這對年輕人獲取可靠資訊帶來哪些挑戰？

articles.title: 施政報告推「人工智能+」行動　大灣區數據協同發展成重點
articles.summary: 香港私隱專員公署全力支持政府在2026年施政報告中提出的「人工智能+」行動計劃，強調善用數據是推動大灣區協同發展的關鍵。公署署長鍾麗玲表示，透過數據要素賦能，可加強香港與內地城市在科技、醫療及教育等領域的合作。與此同時，政府亦計劃在北部都會區推動智慧城市建設，吸引更多科技企業落戶，為年輕人創造更多高質素就業機會，推動香港邁向創新型經濟體。

lv1: 「人工智能+」行動計劃的主要目的是什麼？
哪個政府機構表示全力支持「人工智能+」計劃？
lv2: 大灣區的城市如何透過共享數據來互相幫助？請舉一個生活化的例子說明。
為什麼政府希望吸引科技企業到北部都會區，而不是留在市區？
lv3: 在推動數據共享和人工智能發展的同時，個人私隱應如何受到保障？誰應該負最大責任？
香港年輕人要把握「人工智能+」帶來的就業機會，需要培養哪些能力？現時的學校教育是否足夠準備好他們？
